items.title: Add /resume TUI slash command as an alias of /conversations (APP-5241)
items.body:
## Description
Adds a `/resume` slash command to the Warp Agent CLI / headless TUI that opens the existing conversation history picker — the same UI already reachable via left-arrow on empty input and via `/conversations`.

The agent CLI already has a left-arrow convention for resuming prior conversations (the zero-state hint reads `← for conversations`), but `/resume` is a more discoverable, more intuitive entrypoint.

Implemented as a thin alias, following the `/clear` → `/agent` precedent (a distinct `SlashCommandKind` sharing the existing handler arm):

- New `SlashCommandKind::Resume` and a `RESUME` `StaticCommand` (`TuiOnly`, `AI_ENABLED`, no argument, description "Resume a previous conversation (alias for /conversations)"), registered in the command list so it is discoverable via the slash-command fuzzy filter.
- `SlashCommandKind::Resume` joins the existing `SlashCommandKind::Conversations` arm in the TUI `execute_tui_slash_command`, so it opens the very same `conversation_menu`. No new picker, no new filtering, no new restore path.
- The GUI dispatch match lists `Resume` in its TUI-only bucket.

**Surface choice:** `TuiOnly`. The request is specifically about the agent CLI, the GUI already exposes `/conversations` (with a `cmd-y` / `ctrl-shift-Y` binding), and this matches the `/clear` alias precedent, which is likewise a TUI-only alias of a `GuiAndTui` command.

## Linked Issue
[APP-5241 — TUI: add a `/resume` slash command as an alias of `/conversations`](https://linear.app/warpdotdev/issue/APP-5241/tui-add-a-resume-slash-command-as-an-alias-of-conversations)

Originating Slack thread: https://warpdev.slack.com/archives/C0BDQDW8V5E/p1786109186548789

- [x] Where appropriate, screenshots or a short video of the implementation are included below.

## Testing
- [x] I have manually tested my changes end to end in a live, signed-in TUI (see below).

### Automated tests added
- `resume_command_is_registered_only_for_tui_mode` (`app/.../static_commands/commands_tests.rs`) — `/resume` is registered on the TUI surface and absent from the GUI surface.
- `resume_command_mirrors_conversations_registry_metadata` (same file) — asserts the name, `TuiOnly` surface, no GUI icon, the description, no argument, and that availability / `auto_enter_ai_mode` / argument are **identical to `CONVERSATIONS`**, so the alias can't drift from the command it aliases.
- `resume_slash_command_opens_the_same_conversation_picker_as_conversations` (`crates/warp_tui/src/terminal_session_view_tests.rs`) — typing `/resume` parses to a static slash command, and executing it opens the conversation menu (`TuiInputSuggestionsMode::ConversationMenu`), clears the input, and renders the `Conversations` picker.

### Checks run
- `./script/format` — clean.
- `cargo clippy -p warp -p warp_tui --all-targets --tests -- -D warnings` — clean.
- `cargo nextest run -p warp --lib slash_command` — 127 passed.
- `cargo nextest run --no-fail-fast -p warp_tui` — 958 passed, 1 failed. The single failure is `session::tests::accepts_startup_without_resume`, which is **pre-existing and environmental, not caused by this change**: it asserts `args.api_key == None`, but clap reads `api_key` from `WARP_API_KEY`, which the sandbox sets. It passes under `env -u WARP_API_KEY` (verified).

### Screenshots / Videos
Captured against a live, signed-in internal `local` `warp-tui` build, driven under `tmux` and recorded.

1. **Slash-command menu** — typing `/resume` surfaces the command with the description "Resume a previous conversation (alias for /conversations)". ([still](https://oz.staging.warp.dev/artifacts/019fdc95-f052-7b14-b29b-82989dbd2429))
2. **Conversation picker** — executing it opens the existing `Conversations` inline menu, populated with real history. ([still](https://oz.staging.warp.dev/artifacts/019fdc96-015e-75ac-8670-ad87f23a054d))
3. **Restore** — selecting an entry restores that conversation's transcript via the existing restore path. ([still](https://oz.staging.warp.dev/artifacts/019fdc96-130c-7dc8-9b50-0f58b0eacc5c))

Deterministic `tmux capture-pane` frames of the three states:

```text
  /resume                      Resume a previous conversation (alias for /conversations)
  ▏ > /resume
```

```text
  Conversations
  Simple Math Query Response
  Simple Arithmetic Question
  Simple Arithmetic Question
  Identify Capital Of France
  Identify Capital City
  Identify Capital Of Japan
```

```text
  > what is the capital of Japan?

  Tokyo.

  ∷ 3s
```

**How the proof was captured (honest disclosure).** The sandbox's internal `local` TUI could not start because staging IAP failed *before* user authentication (`Staging IAP access unavailable before startup user authentication`). To get the TUI past startup, the IAP fix from the **separate, not-yet-merged** PR #14796 (`factory/app-5220-nonfatal-iap-local`) was applied to the **local working tree only**. It was **not** committed or pushed: this branch's committed diff is exactly the six files listed above and contains no IAP changes (`app/src/lib.rs` and `app/src/lib_tests.rs` were reverted before pushing). The `/resume` code exercised is exactly this PR's code, but the run did require #14796's fix locally to reach a startable TUI.

items.title: feat(tui): implement TUI input view milestone 1
items.body:
## Description

Implements the TUI input view (Milestone 1) as specified in `specs/tui-input-view/TECH.md`. This is the first functional editor-backed text input for the TUI rendering path.

**What's in this PR:**

### Prerequisite refactor in `crates/editor/` (~580 LOC + ~200 LOC tests, no GUI-path regressions)

- **`ColumnUnit` enum** on `SoftWrapPoint`: replaces the bare `Pixels` column with an explicit `ColumnUnit::Pixels(Pixels)` / `ColumnUnit::Chars(u16)` discriminant so the GUI and TUI coordinate spaces are enforced at the type level (cross-variant ops `debug_assert!`). The ~15 construction sites and `SelectionModel::goal_xs` (now `Option<Vec1<ColumnUnit>>`) / `NavigationResult::goal_x` are updated; `navigate_line` sticky-column logic is unchanged in shape.

- **`LayoutMode` on `RenderState`**: adds `LayoutMode::CharCell(CharCellState)` alongside the existing `LayoutMode::Pixels` path (`CharCellState` holds `terminal_width`, `line_starts`, `total_chars`). In CharCell mode `handle_layout_action` skips font shaping entirely, and `offset_to_softwrap_point` / `softwrap_point_to_offset` / `max_line` use pure char-cell integer arithmetic. New APIs: `RenderState::new_tui(terminal_width, styles, ctx)`, `is_char_cell_mode()`, `update_char_cell_text(text)`, `set_char_cell_terminal_width(width)`. The styles field is retained for API compatibility but unused in CharCell mode.

- **`usize → u32` overflow guard**: `char_cell_softwrap_point_to_offset` treats the final (unbounded) logical line as spanning all remaining rows, so a target row past the end resolves there instead of overflowing. Covered by the round-trip unit tests.

### Editor-backed TUI input (no separate model)

There is **no** `TuiInputModel` — the input reuses the existing `CodeEditorModel` in char-cell mode:

- `app/src/code/editor/model.rs`: adds `CodeEditorModel::new_tui(terminal_width, ctx)` (shares sub-model wiring with the GUI `new()` via a `from_content(..)` helper) and `set_tui_terminal_width(..)`. Its `CoreEditorModel::on_buffer_version_updated` override drives `update_char_cell_text` synchronously on every edit when in char-cell mode (the async font-shaping pipeline is bypassed there). Re-exported for the TUI front-end via `app/src/editor/mod.rs`.

- `crates/warp_tui/src/input/` (~1.2k LOC incl. tests):
  - `kill_buffer.rs`: single-entry kill buffer (Ctrl+K / Ctrl+U / Ctrl+W → Ctrl+Y yank)
  - `view.rs`: `TuiInputView` implementing `TuiView` + `TypedActionView`. Holds `ModelHandle<CodeEditorModel>` plus TUI session state (kill buffer, scroll offset, terminal width, `max_visible_rows = 6`). Full Emacs/readline keybinding dispatch via a `TuiInputAction` enum (Ctrl+A/E/B/F/P/N/K/U/W/Y/H/D/Z, word movement, Shift+arrows, Shift+Enter). Renders via pure char-cell helpers; `TuiInputElement` paints rows, applies `Modifier::REVERSED` to selection spans, and reports the block cursor via `cursor_position()`. Emits `TuiInputViewEvent::Submitted(String)` on Enter.
  - `view_tests.rs`: drives a real `CodeEditorModel` + `TuiInputView`.

### Spec + examples

- `specs/tui-input-view/TECH.md`: as-built architecture spec (design rationale, keybinding table, follow-up scope for runtime wiring, input mode, slash commands, history).
- `crates/warp_tui/examples/tui_input_demo.rs`: interactive editor-backed input demo (`cargo run -p warp_tui --example tui_input_demo`).
- `crates/warpui_core/examples/tui_file_viewer.rs`: validates the TUI rendering/runtime pipeline independently of the editor (scrollable file viewer).

## Linked Issue

N/A — spec-driven feature, see `specs/tui-input-view/TECH.md`

## Testing

- `crates/editor/src/render/model/mod_tests.rs::char_cell`: 12 unit tests (max_line, `offset → point → offset` round-trips at multiple widths, `ColumnUnit::Chars` correctness, multi-line/wrapping boundaries).
- `crates/warp_tui/src/input/view_tests.rs`: 12 tests driving a real `CodeEditorModel` + `TuiInputView` (cursor placement, blank-line navigation, selection text, kill/yank).
- Existing `warp_editor` test suite continues to pass (no GUI-path behaviour changes).
- `./script/format` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --tests -- -D warnings` pass.

Run the examples from a real terminal:
```sh
cargo run -p warp_tui --example tui_input_demo
cargo run -p warpui_core --example tui_file_viewer --features tui -- specs/tui-input-view/TECH.md
```

Wiring `TuiInputView` into the `warp-tui` binary's runtime (today only auth runs there) is the next step.

## Agent Mode
- [x] Warp Agent Mode - This PR was created via Warp's AI Agent Mode

Conversation: https://staging.warp.dev/conversation/c5b70ee0-60c6-49f9-908c-2e3275949d37

CHANGELOG-NEW-FEATURE: TUI input view (Milestone 1): multi-line, Emacs/readline keybindings, editor-backed via CodeEditorModel + SelectionModel + CharCell RenderState

## Description

Warp can now ask the user's real shell to compute completions for the current input line, instead of only consulting its own bundled specs. zsh, bash, fish and PowerShell all compute in the live session and return matches over the existing OSC 9280 protocol, driven through one shared in-band generator-command path. This replaces the zsh-only, Ctrl-Y-triggered round trip described in [CORE-3794](https://linear.app/warpdotdev/issue/CORE-3794/native-shell-completions-drive-all-shells-through-in-band-generator).

`FeatureFlag::NativeShellCompletions` is now in `DOGFOOD_FLAGS`, so the feature is **on for Dev builds** and off for Preview and Stable. Nothing else is needed to switch it on: `app/src/bin/dev.rs` passes `DOGFOOD_FLAGS` to `ChannelState::additional_features()`, which is where `enabled_features()` starts. The `native_shell_completions` cargo feature remains an independent second route for building the path into another channel; it is deliberately not in `app/Cargo.toml`'s `default`, since that would be a Stable promotion.

## Review guide

The risk here is not the completions feature, which is flag-gated. It is the shell bootstrap scripts, which every user runs on every command regardless of the flag. Read in this order:

1. `app/assets/bundled/bootstrap/{bash_body,zsh_body,fish}.sh` — the hex encoder. `warp_hex_encode_string` and its pre-existing call sites are byte-for-byte identical to `master`; the faster encoder is a separate `warp_completions_hex_encode*` function reachable only from the match and description emission sites in each shell's completion loop. That separation is the point: a defect in the new encoder cannot reach the Preexec, Precmd, CommandFinished, DCS/JSON or InitShell hooks.
2. `app/src/terminal/input.rs` — `resolve_completion_sources` and `CompletionSources`, the whole dispatch policy.
3. `crates/warp_terminal/src/model/ansi/mod.rs` and `app/src/terminal/writeable_pty/pty_controller.rs` — the OSC 9280 parsing and the generator write path.

`crates/warp_completer/src/meta.rs` carries a `Span::slice` char-boundary clamp on the shared, flag-independent path. It turns a previously panicking out-of-bounds or non-char-boundary slice into a clamped one and is byte-identical for valid spans.

## What changed

- **All four shells, one path.** PowerShell no longer uses the `Alt+3` / `GetBufferState` key handler; it has a `Warp-Run-GeneratorCommand-NativeCompletion <hex>` function like the others. Its kill-buffer chord stays in its own pty write, and the `9280;S` replacement span with its UTF-16→UTF-8 offset conversion is retained. The start OSC is a bare `9280;A` — the single-valued `incrementally_typed` format parameter is gone end to end.
- **Tab and keybinding only.** Native completions never engage as-you-type; as-you-type keeps Warp's bundled-spec behavior.
- **Two default-on toggles select the sources.** Under **Settings → Features → Terminal Input**, **Warp completions** and **Native shell completions** resolve to one `CompletionSources` policy. Both on: specs first, ask the shell only when they come back empty. Warp on, native off: `master` behavior, including the Tab file-path fallback. Warp off, native on: native only, no specs and no fallback, dispatched up front. Both off: no shell command completions. AI input is always Warp-only.
- **As-you-type is nested under Warp completions**, since it only governs them, and disappears when that toggle is off.
- **The alphabetical re-sort is gone** (`ShellCompletion::sort_by_name` and its only call), so the shell's own emission order reaches the menu. `filter_by_query` still buckets into exact, then prefix, then fuzzy-by-score, and input order is preserved within a bucket.
- **The completions-only encoder keeps every compatibility fix**: bash 3.2's low-byte trim, zsh's `nomultibyte` plus `typeset -g` assignment, the 256-character `od` fallback above which the quadratic loop would stall, and fish's builtin strip of `od`'s output. fish still needs `od` because it has no byte-safe string indexing.

## Decisions

- **Reused OSC 9280** for all four shells rather than the generic OSC 9277 in-band-command channel: smaller diff, and no second output format.
- **Hex-encoded arguments** rather than shell quoting, which removes injection and quoting risk across four shells at once.
- **bash uses `read -ra`, not `eval`**, trading quote fidelity for never executing arbitrary substrings of a partially typed line. A quoted argument containing a space yields zero matches rather than the differently split matches bash's own tokenizer would produce.
- **The fast encoder is scoped to completions rather than shared.** It is measurably faster on the hot path — the completions loop encodes once per match — but the hooks it would otherwise serve run on every command of every session, fork once either way, and are not where the time goes. The shared path therefore keeps `master`'s implementation.

## Explicitly out of scope

- Promoting the flag beyond Dogfood.
- A match cap for pathological completion contexts. Raised with the requester as a policy question.
- Collapsing duplicate matches from the shell (the remaining half of CORE-3800), left at the requester's direction.

## Known issues and limitations

**Tracked, deferred** — each a real bug with its own issue:
- [CORE-3800](https://linear.app/warpdotdev/issue/CORE-3800) — the sorting half is fixed here; **duplicate matches from the shell are still not collapsed**.
- [CORE-3802](https://linear.app/warpdotdev/issue/CORE-3802) — accepted completions are inserted with no shell escaping in bash, so a filename with a space, semicolon or parens inserts as literal text and either fails or splits into two commands. Predates this PR. zsh escapes correctly; bash does not.
- [CORE-3809](https://linear.app/warpdotdev/issue/CORE-3809) — if a request's terminating `9280;B` never arrives (an interrupted request; bash/zsh/fish emit it untrapped), terminal output produced before the next prompt is silently discarded. Measured: the session recovers on its own at the next prompt, exit codes and block commits survive, and the next request is unaffected, so the cost is one command's output.

**Expected behavior given the mechanism, not bugs:**
- A menu opens with **no entry preselected on the first Tab**, so Enter straight after the first Tab submits the raw line. Press Down or Tab again first.
- bash has no description channel (`COMPREPLY` is names only); zsh, fish and PowerShell all resolve descriptions.
- DCS passthrough around zsh's `select` redraw only swallows what precedes the redraw's first ESC byte.
- fish forks `od` once per match, where bash and zsh do not. The obvious builtin fix is unsafe: `string split` yields characters, not bytes, so `中` would encode as `4e2d` rather than `e4b8ad`. The viable route is one `od` per request over the joined candidate list.
- Accepting a candidate containing a control character strips it before insertion, so the inserted text no longer matches the real file. The right fix is at display time — don't offer a candidate the editor cannot insert faithfully.

## Linked Issue
[CORE-3794](https://linear.app/warpdotdev/issue/CORE-3794/native-shell-completions-drive-all-shells-through-in-band-generator).
- [x] The linked issue is labeled `ready-to-spec` or `ready-to-implement`.
- [x] Where appropriate, screenshots or a short video of the implementation are included below.

## Testing

**Integration tests.** The six native-completions integration tests live in stacked PR [#15425](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/pull/15425), not on this branch. Applied to this head additively — 605 insertions, 0 deletions, so master's own changes to the three shared files are preserved — and run once per shell rather than once overall: **24 passed, 0 failed**, six each on bash 5.2.21, zsh 5.9, fish 3.7.0 and PowerShell 7.4.6.

**The encoder split is proven, not asserted.** `warp_hex_encode_string` plus all seven pre-existing call sites across the three shells were extracted from `master` and from this head and diffed: byte-for-byte identical, with a negative control confirming a one-character change to a call site is detected. A 582-case differential — every byte value 1–255 alone and padded, all 255 in one string, the 255/256/257 threshold boundaries, multibyte characters straddling byte 256, invalid UTF-8, leading-dash arguments, OSC framing characters, quotes, backslashes and parens — reports **0 mismatches** between the shared and completions encoders in bash, zsh and fish. Each shell has a negative control that fires.

**Old shells.** Built bash 3.2.57, zsh 5.0.2 and fish 3.1.2 from source. All three bootstrap files parse, and the same 582 cases give 0 disagreements and 0 errors against an independent Python reference. On bash 3.2 the negative control is decisive: removing the low-byte trim produces 271 wrong encodings out of 582, which is what that trim exists to prevent.

**Dogfood gating verified end to end.** A `dev`-channel binary built **without** the `native_shell_completions` cargo feature serves shell-driven completions, which is what proves `DOGFOOD_FLAGS` alone is sufficient. [Capture](https://oz.staging.warp.dev/artifacts/01a03627-ee73-7226-9cdd-4e69d91cb5d4).

**Live terminal behavior with the feature on**, bash and zsh, completion requests interleaved with ordinary commands: session startup, block lifecycle and exit codes, awkward quoting and heredocs, non-ASCII, `seq 1 5000`, carriage-return progress, Ctrl-C, history and tab titles. No stray OSC text, hex runs or duplicated blocks anywhere. Command lengths of 190, 193, 194, 195, 200, 255, 256, 257 and 4096 characters all render correctly with no perceptible pause. The recordings and screenshots above are that pass.

Not covered: Windows and conpty, which no runner in the pool can reach, and where the PowerShell command execution this adds carries its risk.

- [x] I have manually tested my changes locally — via `cargo build --bin dev --features gui` and launching the resulting binary under Xvfb, which is what `./script/run` builds for this channel.

### Screenshots / Videos
At the top of this description.

Warp can now ask the user's real shell to compute completions for the current input line, instead of only consulting its own bundled specs. zsh, bash, fish and PowerShell all compute in the live session and return matches over the existing OSC 9280 protocol, driven through one shared in-band generator-command path. The risk here is not the completions feature, which is flag-gated. It is the shell bootstrap scripts, which every user runs on every command regardless of the flag. Read in this order:

1. `app/assets/bundled/bootstrap/{bash_body,zsh_body,fish}.sh` — the hex encoder. `warp_hex_encode_string` and its pre-existing call sites are byte-for-byte identical to `master`; the faster encoder is a separate `warp_completions_hex_encode*` function reachable only from the match and description emission sites in each shell's completion loop. 2. `app/src/terminal/input.rs` — `resolve_completion_sources` and `CompletionSources`, the whole dispatch policy.
3. `app/src/terminal/model/ansi/mod.rs` and `pty_controller.rs` — the OSC 9280 parsing and the generator write path.

`crates/warp_completer/src/meta.rs` carries a `Span::slice` char-boundary clamp on the shared, flag-independent path. It turns a previously panicking out-of-bounds or non-char-boundary slice into a clamped one and is byte-identical for valid spans.

- **All four shells, one path.** PowerShell no longer uses the `Alt+3` / `GetBufferState` key handler; it has a `Warp-Run-GeneratorCommand-NativeCompletion <hex>` function like the others. The start OSC is a bare `9280;A` — the single-valued `incrementally_typed` format parameter is gone end to end.
- **Tab and keybinding only.** Native completions never engage as-you-type; as-you-type keeps Warp's bundled-spec behavior.
- **Two default-on toggles select the sources.** Under **Settings → Features → Terminal Input**, **Warp completions** and **Native shell completions** resolve to one `CompletionSources` policy. Warp off, native on: native only, no specs and no fallback, dispatched up front. Both off: no shell command completions. AI input is always Warp-only.
- **As-you-type is nested under Warp completions**, since it only governs them, and disappears when that toggle is off.
- **The alphabetical re-sort is gone** (`ShellCompletion::sort_by_name` and its only call), so the shell's own emission order reaches the menu. `filter_by_query` still buckets into exact, then prefix, then fuzzy-by-score, and input order is preserved within a bucket.
- **The completions-only encoder keeps every compatibility fix**: bash 3.2's low-byte trim, zsh's `nomultibyte` plus `typeset -g` assignment, the 256-character `od` fallback above which the quadratic loop would stall, and fish's builtin strip of `od`'s output. fish still needs `od` because it has no byte-safe string indexing.

The shared path therefore keeps `master`'s implementation.

## Explicitly out of scope

- Promoting the flag beyond Dogfood.
- A match cap for pathological completion contexts. Raised with the requester as a policy question.
- Collapsing duplicate matches from the shell (the remaining half of CORE-3800), left at the requester's direction.

## Known issues and limitations

**Tracked, deferred** — each a real bug with its own issue:
- [CORE-3800](https://linear.app/warpdotdev/issue/CORE-3800) — the sorting half is fixed here; **duplicate matches from the shell are still not collapsed**.

## Linked Issue

Applied to this head and run: `cargo nextest run -p integration -E 'test(shell_integration_tests) and (test(native_shell_completion) or test(native_completions))'` → **6 passed, 0 failed**, with zsh, bash, fish and PowerShell 7.4.6 all installed. items.title: Double ctrl-c to exit TUI
items.body:
## Description

### 1. View-level keybindings for the TUI

This PR introduces GUI-style, view-level keybinding registration for the TUI and moves all TUI key handling onto it. The TUI runtime's keymap pass (`TuiScreen::dispatch_event`) already worked end-to-end for TUI views — it was just unused. Now:

- **Per-module `init(app)` fns** (GUI convention), aggregated in `crates/warp_tui/src/keybindings.rs` and called once at TUI startup:
  - `input::init` — the entire readline/chord editing table as user-remappable `EditableBinding`s named `tui:input:*` (submit, newline, deletion, word ops, movement, selection, kill/yank, undo/redo). Printable-character insertion stays element-level, matching the GUI.
  - `terminal_session_view::init` / `root_view::init` — fixed (non-remappable) `ctrl-c` bindings (see below).
- **Responder-chain ordering**: the session view now focuses the input view, so the chain is `[root, session, input]`. Deepest-first matching means input bindings win for keys they define, and unbound keys (ctrl-c) fall through to session, then root.
- **Cross-surface isolation**: GUI bindings cannot fire in the TUI — predicate-scoped bindings never match TUI keymap contexts, and even predicate-less bindings dispatch action types no TUI view handles, so the keystroke falls through to the element pass (covered by a new runtime test). Debug-time validators (`register_tui_binding_validator`) additionally require every keystroke binding matching a TUI context to be TUI-owned (`tui:` name prefix or the `tui` binding group), which also prevents permissive multi-keystroke chords from swallowing prefix keys via pending matches. TUI→GUI leakage is structurally impossible (`warp_tui` isn't linked into the GUI binary).
- **Supporting framework changes**: the TUI driver no longer force-terminates on ctrl-c (the intercept is removed; ctrl-c flows through normal dispatch); crossterm shift+letter keystrokes are normalized to uppercase to match `Keystroke::parse` conventions; `TuiEventHandler::new` takes a boxed child.

User customization is a follow-up: the `tui:input:*` names are the stable contract, so enabling `keybindings.yaml` overrides later is just loading them in the TUI bootstrap. Scoping/plan: [TUI view-level keybindings with surface isolation](https://staging.warp.dev/drive/notebook/i9aK59jtus7yfuh8rZhMlR).

### 2. Double ctrl-c to exit (single ctrl-c cancels / clears)

Built on the bindings above, ctrl-c now matches peer agent CLIs (Claude Code, Amp) instead of hard-exiting the TUI:

- **Single ctrl-c** performs one contextual action, in priority order: cancel the running agent conversation (streams + tool calls, with a fresh-conversation guard) → clear a non-empty input → no-op.
- **Every press arms a 1s exit-confirmation window** (`ExitConfirmation`, a context-free unit-tested state machine); a **second press within the window exits** unconditionally. Typing into the input disarms it.
- A new one-row dim **footer below the input shows `ctrl-c again to exit`** while armed (placeholder for the fuller footer design; auto-hides on expiry).
- **Pre-session screens** (login placeholder / failure) keep single-ctrl-c-to-exit via the root view's `ExitApp` binding, so the app is always exitable.

Specs checked in at `specs/tui-ctrl-c/PRODUCT.md` and `specs/tui-ctrl-c/TECH.md`.
